title: Fretboard system
summary: Barre chords, every note on every string, the five movable chord forms, and triads and inversions on string sets.

lessons.title: Barre chords: the E form
lessons.summary: Turn the open E and Em fingerings into movable barre chords rooted on string 6.

steps.title: Your finger as a nut
steps.body:
A **barre** is one finger laid flat across several strings. In a **barre chord**, finger 1 barres a whole fret and acts like a movable nut. The other fingers make an open-chord fingering above it.

Take the open **E** chord, refinger it with fingers 2, 3, and 4, and slide it up one fret. Barre fret 1 with finger 1. Every note is now a half step higher: E becomes **F**.

- Finger 1: barre all six strings at fret 1.
- Finger 3: string 5, fret 3.
- Finger 4: string 4, fret 3.
- Finger 2: string 3, fret 2.

This is the **E-form barre**. Its root is on **string 6**, under the barre.

steps.title: Making the barre ring
steps.body:
Barre chords take weeks to sound clean. That is normal.

- Put the barre right behind the fret, and roll finger 1 slightly onto its bony outer edge.
- Thumb low behind the neck, roughly behind finger 2. Pull back gently with the arm instead of squeezing with the thumb.
- Only strings 6, 2, and 1 depend on the barre in the major form; the other fingers cover the rest. Check those three first.
- Fret 1 is the hardest spot. Practice at fret 5 first, where the string tension is lower.

steps.title: Naming barre chords
steps.body:
The chord is named after the note under the barre on string 6. You learned those notes in Stage 1:

| Fret | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chord | F | G | A | B | C | D |

For **minor**, use the Em fingering instead: lift finger 2, so the barre plays string 3 as the minor third. F at fret 1 becomes **Fm**; at fret 3, **Gm**.

diagram.caption: Gm, E-form minor barre at fret 3.

steps.title: F, Fm, G, Gm
steps.caption: E-form major and minor at frets 1 and 3.

exercise.prompt: E-form barre chords: F (fret 1), G (fret 3), A (fret 5), then Am (fret 5, minor form).

mistakeTips: Pick each string slowly to find the dead one; usually it is string 3 or 2 under a knuckle crease. Shift the barre slightly up or down.
The app grades pitch only, so an open G also counts. Use the barre on purpose; it is what makes the fingering movable.
Rest between tries. Squeezing harder rarely helps; better placement does.

questions.prompt: Where is the root of an E-form barre chord?
questions.explanation: Strings 6 and 1 are both the root, and string 4 an octave above string 6.

questions.prompt: E-form major barre at fret 5. What chord?
E-form minor barre at fret 7. What chord?
How do you turn the E-form major into minor?
choices: Move the barre up one fret
questions.explanation: With finger 2 off, the barre plays string 3 a half step lower: the minor third.

questions.prompt: Which chord is an E-form barre at fret 8?

reviewItems.prompt: Play F as an E-form barre at fret 1.

lessons.title: Barre chords: the A form
lessons.summary: Move the A and Am fingerings up the neck with a barre, rooted on string 5.

steps.title: The A-form barre
steps.body:
Do the same with the open **A** chord. Barre finger 1 across strings 5 to 1 and put the A fingering two frets higher.

**Bb** at fret 1: finger 1 barres strings 5–1 at fret 1; strings 4, 3, 2 at fret 3. Many players flatten finger 3 across all three strings at fret 3; others use fingers 2, 3, 4. Do not strum string 6.

The root is on **string 5**, under the barre.

steps.title: A-form minor
steps.body:
From the **Am** fingering: barre strings 5–1, finger 3 on string 4, finger 4 on string 3 (two frets up), finger 2 on string 2 (one fret up).

**Bm** at fret 2: strings 5 and 1 on the barre at fret 2; string 4 fret 4; string 3 fret 4; string 2 fret 3. This is the chord that appears as vi in D major and ii in A major, so you will use it a lot.

| Fret on string 5 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chord | Bb | B | C | D | E |

diagram.caption: Bm, A-form minor barre at fret 2.

steps.title: I–vi–IV–V in D
steps.caption: D, Bm, G, A. Bm is the A-form barre at fret 2.

exercise.prompt: A-form barre chords: Bm (fret 2), C (fret 3), Cm (fret 3), D (fret 5).

mistakeTips: The barre only needs to press strings 5 and 1 hard; the other fingers cover the middle.
Mute string 6 with the tip of finger 1 touching it.
If the high E is dead in the major form, lift finger 3's knuckle or use fingers 2-3-4.

exercise.prompt: I–vi in D: D to Bm and back for one minute.

mistakeTips: Place the barre first, then the other fingers.
Aim for a clean strum over speed. Barre changes take longer to settle.

questions.prompt: Where is the root of an A-form barre chord?
A-form major at fret 3. What chord?
A-form minor at fret 7. What chord?
You need F#m. Which barre?
questions.explanation: F# is at fret 2 on string 6.

reviewItems.prompt: Two ways to play C as a barre chord?
reviewItems.answer: A-form at fret 3 or E-form at fret 8.

lessons.title: Every note on every string
lessons.summary: Use octave patterns to find any note on strings 4, 3, 2, and 1 from the root strings you already know.

steps.title: Octave patterns across the neck
steps.body:
You know strings 6 and 5. Octave patterns carry that knowledge to the other strings:

- **String 6 → string 4** and **string 5 → string 3**: two strings up, **two** frets up.
- **String 4 → string 2** and **string 3 → string 1**: two strings up, **three** frets up. The pattern shifts because the B string is tuned a major 3rd above G instead of a 4th.
- **String 6 and string 1** are both E: the same fret gives the same note name, two octaves apart.

Example for C: string 5 fret 3 → string 3 fret 5 → string 1 fret 8. And string 6 fret 8 → string 4 fret 10 → string 2 fret 13. (String 2 fret 1 is also C, one octave lower.)

steps.title: Landmarks on the other strings
steps.body:
Natural notes on the remaining strings (frets 0–12):

- **String 4 (D):** D 0, E 2, F 3, G 5, A 7, B 9, C 10, D 12
- **String 3 (G):** G 0, A 2, B 4, C 5, D 7, E 9, F 10, G 12
- **String 2 (B):** B 0, C 1, D 3, E 5, F 6, G 8, A 10, B 12
- **String 1 (E):** same as string 6

You do not need to memorize these as lists. Use octave patterns and the fact that frets 5 and 7 match the next string up (fret 4 onto the B string).

exercise.prompt: Fretboard Hunt: play C in every octave you can find within 60 seconds. Try to use a different string each time.

mistakeTips: C3: string 5 fret 3 or string 6 fret 8.
C4: string 3 fret 5, string 2 fret 1, or string 4 fret 10.
C5: string 1 fret 8.

exercise.prompt: Fretboard Hunt: every F# within 60 seconds.

mistakeTips: F#2: string 6 fret 2. F#3: string 4 fret 4, or string 5 fret 9.
F#4: string 1 fret 2, or string 2 fret 7.
Use the octave patterns: string 6 fret 2 → string 4 fret 4.

questions.prompt: A on string 3, fret 2. Where is the A an octave higher on string 1?
questions.explanation: From string 3 to string 1: two strings up, three frets up.

questions.prompt: What note is at string 2, fret 8?
questions.explanation: B C D E F G: B 0, C 1, D 3, E 5, F 6, G 8.

questions.prompt: What note is at string 4, fret 9?

reviewItems.prompt: Octave pattern from string 4 to string 2?
reviewItems.answer: Two strings up, three frets up.

lessons.title: Five movable chord forms
lessons.summary: Play C major in five places up the neck using the C, A, G, E, and D forms, and see how they link.

steps.title: Every open chord is a movable form
steps.body:
The barre chords you learned are the E and A open fingerings moved up the neck. The same works for C, G, and D. Together these are the **five movable chord forms**, often called the **CAGED** system after their order.

For any chord, the five forms appear up the neck in the order **C → A → G → E → D**, then repeat. Each form overlaps the next: the top of one is the bottom of the next.

Here is **C major** in all five forms.

steps.title: C form and A form
steps.body:
**C form** (open position): the C chord you know. Root on string 5 fret 3 and string 2 fret 1.

**A form** (fret 3): the A-form barre. Root on string 5 fret 3 and string 3 fret 5.

diagram.caption: C major, A form at fret 3.

steps.title: G form
steps.body:
**G form** (frets 5–8): the open G fingering moved up. Root on string 6 fret 8, string 3 fret 5, and string 1 fret 8.

The full six-string version is a big stretch; players usually use just part of it, such as strings 4, 3, 2 at fret 5 plus string 1 at fret 8.

steps.title: E form and D form
steps.body:
**E form** (fret 8): the E-form barre. Root on string 6 fret 8, string 4 fret 10, string 1 fret 8.

**D form** (frets 10–13): the open D fingering moved up, strings 4 to 1. Root on string 4 fret 10 and string 2 fret 13.

After the D form comes the C form again, at fret 12. The cycle repeats.

diagram.caption: C major, E form at fret 8.

steps.title: Using the forms
steps.body:
Any major chord works the same way. Find its root in one form and the others follow in order. For **G major**: E form at fret 3, D form at fret 5, C form at fret 7, A form at fret 10, G form at fret 12 (and open).

Why it helps:

- You can play a chord in the part of the neck where you already are.
- Each form contains the chord's arpeggio, and the matching scale fits around it. Stage 8 builds solos on this.

steps.title: C major up the neck
steps.caption: The same chord in the C, A, G, E, and D forms.

exercise.prompt: Arpeggio the A form (fret 3) and then the E form (fret 8) of C: play each string low to high.

mistakeTips: Hold the whole chord while you pick each string, so the notes ring together.
A form starts on string 5, E form on string 6.
Say chord tones as you go: root, 5th, root, 3rd, 5th.

exercise.prompt: D form of C (frets 10–13): play strings 4 to 1.

mistakeTips: Finger 1 on string 4 fret 10 takes the place of the open D string; the other fingers make the open D fingering ten frets higher (frets 12, 13, 12).
Past fret 12 the frets are narrow; keep fingertips close to the fret wire.

questions.prompt: In what order do the five forms appear going up the neck?
questions.explanation: C → A → G → E → D, then repeat.

questions.prompt: Which form comes after the E form going up?
G major as an E form is at fret 3. Which form comes next above it?
Which two forms are the familiar barre chords?
questions.explanation: E form (root on 6) and A form (root on 5).

reviewItems.prompt: Order of the five movable chord forms up the neck?
reviewItems.answer: C A G E D (then repeat).

reviewItems.prompt: C major as an A form is at which fret? As an E form?
reviewItems.answer: A form at fret 3; E form at fret 8.

lessons.title: Triads on string sets and inversions
lessons.summary: Play three-note triads on adjacent strings, and hear root position, first inversion, and second inversion.

steps.title: Inversions
steps.body:
A triad has three notes, so any of them can be at the bottom:

- **Root position**: root lowest. C E G.
- **First inversion**: third lowest. E G C. Written **C/E**.
- **Second inversion**: fifth lowest. G C E. Written **C/G**.

A symbol with a slash is a **slash chord**: the chord, then the bass note. Inversions sound like the same chord with a different weight. Root position is the most solid; inversions sound lighter and are useful for smooth bass lines.

steps.title: Triads on strings 3, 2, 1
steps.body:
A **string set** is a group of adjacent strings. On strings 3-2-1, the three inversions of C climb the neck:

| Voicing | Frets (3, 2, 1) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| second inversion | 0, 1, 0 | G C E |
| root position | 5, 5, 3 | C E G |
| first inversion | 9, 8, 8 | E G C |
| second inversion | 12, 13, 12 | G C E |

These small voicings cut through a band or a second guitar and are easy to move.

steps.title: Triads on strings 4, 3, 2
steps.body:
The same idea one string set lower:

| Voicing | Frets (4, 3, 2) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| first inversion | 2, 0, 1 | E G C |
| second inversion | 5, 5, 5 | G C E |
| root position | 10, 9, 8 | C E G |

Notice how each voicing sits inside one of the five chord forms. Triads are the chord forms trimmed to three strings.

steps.title: Three inversions of C
steps.caption: Root position, first inversion, second inversion.

exercise.prompt: Strings 3-2-1: play C root position (frets 5, 5, 3), first inversion (9, 8, 8), then second inversion (12, 13, 12), one note at a time.

mistakeTips: Root position: finger 3 and 4 at fret 5 on strings 3 and 2, finger 1 at fret 3 on string 1. Or barre fret 5 lightly.
First inversion: strings 2 and 1 at fret 8 (finger 1 barre), string 3 at fret 9 (finger 2).
Second inversion: strings 3 and 1 at fret 12, string 2 at fret 13.

exercise.prompt: Play G major three ways on strings 3-2-1: frets 4-3-3 (G/B), 7-8-7 (G/D), 12-12-10 (G).

mistakeTips: G/B: B on string 3 fret 4, D on string 2 fret 3, G on string 1 fret 3.
G/D: D on string 3 fret 7, G on string 2 fret 8, B on string 1 fret 7.
G: G on string 3 fret 12, B on string 2 fret 12, D on string 1 fret 10.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest note of C/E?
questions.explanation: The note after the slash is the bass.

questions.prompt: A C chord with G in the bass is in…
questions.explanation: The fifth in the bass = second inversion.

questions.prompt: Which inversion puts the third in the bass?
Listen. Root position or an inversion?
questions.explanation: That was C/G: G is the lowest note.

questions.prompt: Listen. Root position or an inversion?
questions.explanation: That was G B D with G lowest.

reviewItems.prompt: Spell C in first inversion and give its symbol.
C root position on strings 3-2-1: which frets?

lessons.title: Fretboard review: House of the Rising Sun
lessons.summary: Review barre chords, chord forms, and inversions, then play the full traditional progression with a real F.

steps.title: What you know now
steps.body:
- **E-form** barre: root on string 6. **A-form** barre: root on string 5.
- Octave patterns find any note on any string.
- Five movable chord forms, **C A G E D**, cover the neck for any chord.
- Triads on string sets, and inversions: root position, first (3rd in bass), second (5th in bass).

questions.prompt: E-form minor barre at fret 5?
A-form major at fret 7?
Which is a first-inversion D chord?
questions.explanation: The third of D is F#.

questions.prompt: What note is at string 3, fret 10?
C major as a G form sits around which frets?

exercise.prompt: Barre warm-up: Am to F (E-form barre at fret 1) and back, one minute.

mistakeTips: Every finger moves. Land the barre and finger 3 (string 5, fret 3) first, then the rest.
If fret 1 is too hard today, play the change with Fmaj7 and come back to it tomorrow.

steps.title: House of the Rising Sun
steps.body:
The full traditional progression, 16 measures in 3/4, one chord per measure:

**Am C D F | Am C E E | Am C D F | Am E Am E**

Use the E-form barre for F. Strum three downstrokes per measure, or use the arpeggio pattern from the Fingerstyle branch.

steps.title: House of the Rising Sun (traditional), chords
steps.caption: Three strums per measure. F is a full barre chord this time.

reviewItems.answer: Am C D F | Am C E E | Am C D F | Am E Am E
